neighbours.label: A person's given name used as part of the name of an institution or place named after them (the 'John' in 'John Wayne Airport', 'Eduardo' in 'Eduardo Mondlane University'), not the same name referring to the person.
fire: Our flight lands at George Bush Intercontinental Airport at noon.
He earned his degree at the Thomas Jefferson University in Philadelphia.
The children played all afternoon in Martin Luther King Park.
She works as a nurse at the Mary Washington Hospital.
The ferry leaves from the pier near Simon Bolivar Square.
The talk will take place at the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation offices.
Our school trip ended at the Anne Frank House museum.
The game was played at the Ernst Happel Stadium in Vienna.
quiet: Our flight lands near the town where George Bush grew up.
He wrote his thesis on Thomas Jefferson and the early republic.
The children read a book about Martin Luther King in class.
She wrote a biography of Mary Washington, mother of the president.
The ferry carried a statue of Simon Bolivar across the river.
The talk was given by Robert Wood, a retired banker.
Our school trip ended with a reading from the diary of Anne Frank.
The game was coached by Ernst Happel for many years.

short: given name inside an eponymous institution
notes: Probes (fraction of max 68.5): 'at the Eduardo Mondlane University' 0.625, 'at John Wayne Airport' 0.623, 'the Jean Mayer … Research Center' 0.764, 'in Lillian Bryant Park' 0.502, all on the given name. Same names as people: 'Eduardo Mondlane led' 0.010, 'John Wayne starred' 0.023, 'My friend Jean' 0.008; unnamed 'national university' 0.026. Near misses keep the person and the sentence frame.
